pick.headline: Former KGB chief Yuriy Andropov becomes Soviet leader
pick.summary: On November 12, 1982, the Central Committee elected Yuriy Andropov General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, two days after Brezhnev's death.
pick.significance: Andropov had headed the KGB for fifteen years. His accession put an intelligence chief at the top of the Soviet system during one of the tensest periods of the Cold War.
pick.fbis: Sofia's Horizont radio broke into its program on November 12, 1982: it had just received the news from Moscow that the Central Committee had elected Andropov general secretary.

alternates.headline: Indonesian troops fire on mourners in Dili
alternates.summary: On November 12, 1991, Indonesian troops opened fire on a funeral procession turned independence demonstration at the Santa Cruz cemetery in Dili, East Timor, killing many.
alternates.significance: Filmed by a foreign journalist, the massacre turned international attention to Indonesia's occupation of East Timor and strained its relations with Washington.
alternates.fbis: The East Asia report of November 12, 1991, carried AFP's same-day dispatch from Jakarta that Indonesian soldiers had fired on a crowd of mourners at a cemetery in Dili.
